items.title: Longineu Parsons interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 17, 2026
items.q: So I went back and said hello. We all hung out, we had a nice little hang there.

ctx.x: Well I wanted to bring up a couple of people. First of all I was looking at your list of folks you’ve had associations with and my job is actually named after Joe Williams. I am the Joe Williams Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive, and he helped us get this project off the ground. Do you have memories with him?

Yeah, yes, yes. I do have memories of Joe Williams. I loved his whole style, his way of being on stage. I mean yeah he was something else. And see when I was coming up as a musician my mother always said, “You know I hope you get to –” she said her favorite singer was Joe Williams. So she was saying she would hope that maybe I would get to play with him someday, or know him or something like that. Or you know get to check him out live or something. So my mother was visiting me in New York and it happened ©…

that Joe Williams was playing at a club there. So I said, “Hey Mom, we’re going out tonight.” And then she said, “Well where are we going?” I said, “You don’t worry about it,” you know, “just come on.” And then as we are getting ready she said, “Oh where is he playing?” She knew that that must have been why I was taking her out. So I said, “Yeah, okay you got it.” So I tipped the maître d – I guess he wouldn’t have been maître d – the waiter or the guy who met us there because – was it a restaurant? Yeah, maybe.…
